sample.identity: Configured x86 Cobalt Strike DNS Beacon reflective DLL

method: Independent static disassembly and execution-path tracing with Rizin, cleave facts including decoded strings, manual XOR/TLV decoding, and atomscan before/after. No sample executed or C2 contacted. Comparison specimens fetched with forager; originals and provenance remain in scratch.
behavior_evidence: MZRE bootstrap calls the raw ReflectiveLoader export at 0x9436. VA 0x1000a036 maps the image, resolves imports, applies relocations, adjusts permissions and calls its mapped entry point at 0x1000a208. The ordinary entry dispatches through 0x10019ae6 to 0x10009f78.

Initialization at VA 0x1000bab6 calls 0x1000bf13. The latter decodes a separate 2048-byte block with XOR 0x8a at 0x1000bf3c. Initialization then XORs 6144 bytes at VA 0x10035020 (raw 0x33a20) with 0x2e at 0x1000bc6e, parses typed records into its settings array, and clears the source at 0x1000bdba. The first 4096 decoded bytes contain the normal Beacon settings, independently parsed in scratch/config.json.

Recovered settings: DNS mode 1, port 53, interval 10000 ms, jitter 0, idle value 8.4.4.4, ns1.blueorbits.site and /api/v1/telemetry, RSA public key, and wmiprvse.exe/msedge.exe spawn paths. These are configuration facts, not claims of contact or actual process creation.

The main loop at VA 0x1000440d queries tasking through 0x10002f37. Native DNS wrapper 0x10002e92 calls DnsQuery_A at 0x10002edf. At 0x1000461b the decoded control value is XORed against the idle word, checked against F0 and fetch-mode flags; task bytes are obtained by A/AAAA/TXT branches, authenticated/decrypted through 0x1000b43b, and passed at 0x10004695 to 0x10009ae2.

VA 0x10009ae2 parses network-order command and size fields, bounds-checks records and dispatches through 0x10009446. The latter uses a 117-entry opcode jump table at 0x1000945d; case 1 reaches process handler 0x10005bed. Handlers retain process launch, file and directory operations, token manipulation, and remote execution capabilities.

Remote memory writer 0x1000d3a3 calls WriteProcessMemory at 0x1000d42c. Thread helper 0x1000cd72 uses CreateRemoteThread at 0x1000ce29 when supplied a process handle; callers include remote-execution code at 0x100066bd/0x10006726 and 0x1000d507/0x1000d545. This establishes executable implementation rather than import-name co-occurrence.

Named-pipe handler reads from its connected pipe, calls ImpersonateNamedPipeClient at 0x100047ce and opens the impersonated thread token at 0x100047ea. This establishes token impersonation capability; no successful elevation is asserted.

Reflective-loader header copier 0x1000a576 copies the headers, tests the characteristics flag, then clears the mapped PE signature at 0x1000a5c1, DOS magic at 0x1000a5cc and e_lfanew at 0x1000a5d2. The supplied image enables the tested flag. The new suspicious rule detects this linked erasure sequence.
judgment: Likely malicious when found on a machine: this is a configured covert tasking implant with reflective execution, header erasure, process injection and token impersonation, not an ordinary application DLL or inert reference to Beacon. Cobalt Strike also supports authorized assessments. No engagement authorization, parent package, installation chain, or deployment context was supplied; a public-registry origin alone does not establish benign use. Verdict follows behavior and packaging, not scanner scores or feed claims.
finding_review: Retain native DNS tasking and MZRE reflective Beacon detections; both are corroborated by executable paths. Retain suspicious relocation-header contradiction and Beacon diagnostic identity. The former literally matches contradictory header fields; it does not claim that this alone proves maliciousness.

Retain ordinary imported API capabilities, including debugging, execution, networking, crypto-provider acquisition/release, memory access, privileges and tokens. IsDebuggerPresent is present in CRT code; its notable reference findings do not claim a hostile analysis gate.

Encoded-string candidates are leads: percent decoding of printf formats and accidental XOR strings are not proof of obfuscation. The manually traced XOR initialization establishes the actual data transformation.

changes.action: Remove unsupported hostile composite; retain all atomic matchers
changes.reason: An ordinary CRT case-fold table is not a decoder. Its other legs are an indirect call and unbound stack arguments. In this specimen the stack signature calls CreateFileMappingA with INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE, not a current-process protection API. There is no matcher-bound transformed-buffer-to-execution relationship.

changes.action: Move/rename without changing matcher, platform, type, size, architecture, confidence or criticality
changes.reason: The required observation is the 0x40/-1 argument operands; no API or handle role is bound. Operand is the specific subject, as for the neighboring third-stack-argument-0x40 rule. It is no longer accepted as proof of executable-page protection.

changes.action: Retain matcher, scope, proximity and exclusions as a notable API/code profile
changes.reason: A VirtualProtectEx reference near unbound call signatures establishes co-occurrence, not that a data buffer becomes executable and is called. Remove unsupported T1620 execution mapping.

changes.action: Preserve matcher and scope; move to neutral telemetry-route leaf
changes.reason: A literal telemetry/beacon API path establishes neither C2 traffic nor a request. All three exact local consumers now reference the neutral atom.

changes.action: Preserve matcher/scope/severity; correct name/description and consumer; remove T1041
changes.reason: The path occurs in this native Windows DLL. It identifies neither QNX nor .NET and proves no exfiltration.

changes.action: Preserve matcher/scope/severity and both exact consumers
changes.reason: GetUserNameA names an account lookup rather than a hostname query.

changes.action: Add notable direction-neutral XOR loop signature
changes.reason: Live 2048/6144-byte transforms use register bounds, unlike the existing distinct 4096-byte immediate-bound loop. Key, address and bound value are not sample-specific requirements.

changes.action: Add suspicious mapped-image signature-erasure code detection
changes.reason: One code sequence links the PE-header pointer and zeroing of PE signature, DOS magic and e_lfanew. No family/domain/configuration token is required.

consumer_audit: Searched exact IDs and every ancestor selector before changes. The removed decoding composite has no exact external YAML consumers. Ancestor consumers are PHP/JavaScript/TypeScript scoped and cannot consume its PE-only match.

Raw operand atom exact consumers were the removed composite, fiber profile, executable-page-protection-evidence and x86-virtualprotectex-data-dispatch. Fiber profile retains the relocated operand. Executable-page-protection-evidence drops the unsupported API inference; protection API and stronger argument atoms remain. Its JIT consumer can no longer be satisfied solely by this unbound stack signature.

Broad mem/protect selectors intentionally stop treating unbound arguments as protection. No sample-level API coverage is lost; the relocated notable operand remains. The moved nearby-call profile has no exact consumers; broad fileless selectors lose only an unestablished fileless execution claim.

Telemetry route ancestor C2 consumers include JavaScript-only composites and a CrystalX PE exclusion gated to 5-15 MB, disjoint from the atom maximum of 5 MB. They gain no new behavior from a neutral route. Exact native beacon consumers retain the route condition unchanged.

Username exact consumers in Go loader-hook and Telegram recon profiles were updated. Broad sysinfo consumers are JavaScript/Perl scoped and cannot consume this PE/DLL-only atom. Newly visible user/lookup ancestor memberships remain account-name capability observations.
No new taxonomy directories were introduced. Every destination is an existing leaf, within its reviewed budget. Changes retain evidence rather than adding score-oriented duplicate rules.

validation.benign_control: Existing real NSIS nsexec DLL: identical 29 findings before/after; no new suspicious/hostile match.
validation.external_results: Current cleave retains DNS-tasking, reflective Beacon and third-party attack signatures on both unchanged original malformed-PE variants. Separate PE-signature-restored analysis copies (not originals) remain atomscan malicious at probability 0.99. The copies are explicitly not reconstructed originals.
validation.material_losses: One unsupported hostile decoding/execution composite removed from this sample. Four other lost IDs are semantic relocations/renames with preserved matchers. The unchanged accurate baseline ASCII-case-fold matcher no longer surfaces in atomscan because its firing consumer was removed; its bytes and rule remain, and the actual XOR transformation is now detected. No supported DNS-tasking, injection, execution, token or crypto API detection was lost. Shared nearby-call profile loses only unsupported hostile/data-flow claims.
validation.disagreements: No final verdict disagreement for the supplied sample. The installed atomscan 2.13.0 misroutes comparison originals with corrupted PE signatures as unknown (one measured probability 0.00002414), while current cleave recognizes them as PE and detects the attacks. Header-normalized copies recover atomscan coverage. This is an engine/classifier routing gap, not a reason to retain inaccurate YAML.
validation.final_gate: make validate, run as the final action after review and marker creation
